$comment: Labelled cases for bin/eval-web-search.js. This is the only artefact that
measures the FEATURE rather than the code: the decision to search lives
inside the model, so no unit test can tell you whether 'auto' is tuned
right. Six categories, because each one fails differently and each one
expectSearch is the label. For category C it is deliberately true even
where the model probably 'knows' the answer: remembering a version or a
price correctly as of training is not the same as it still being true.
needsCorpus marks cases that only mean anything against a real
meeting_history.db with relevant content. Edit their questions to match
your own meetings before trusting their results.

categories.A: Stable concept — must NOT search. Failures here are pure waste and are the likeliest default-tuning problem.
categories.B: Current fact — MUST search. Failure means a confidently stale answer, the worst outcome in the set.
categories.C: Mutable but plausibly known — MUST search. The category that justifies not waiting for the model to say 'I don't know'.
categories.D: Explicit request — MUST search. Failure is a broken promise, not a judgement call.
categories.E: Internal only — must NOT search. The answer is in the team's own records.
categories.F: Both — MUST search, and must also cite internal evidence.
